general_background.title: Oleylamine changes how sulfur is delivered
general_background.summary: An amine can convert elemental sulfur into soluble polysulfide species before metal sulfide nanocrystals form. How sulfur is made available from that solution affects whether new nuclei form or existing particles keep growing.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: From Sulfur−Amine Solutions to Metal Sulfide Nanocrystals: Peering into the Oleylamine−Sulfur Black Box

general_background.title: Alkylamine coordination and exchange
general_background.summary: Dodecylamine can bind surface metal sites in colloidal cadmium chalcogenide syntheses. Replacing a labile amine with a more strongly binding ligand changes surface chemistry and can change how the particles disperse.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Influence of Thiol Capping on the Exciton Luminescence and Decay Kinetics of CdTe and CdSe Quantum Dots

general_background.title: Zinc halide changes the coordination environment
general_background.summary: A zinc halide additive can participate in the coordination chemistry of aminophosphine-based indium phosphide growth without being the phosphorus source. That environment can change the growth and surface chemistry of the resulting nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Aminophosphines: A Double Role in the Synthesis of Colloidal Indium Phosphide Quantum Dots

general_background.title: Stable cluster intermediates can delay particle growth
general_background.summary: In some indium phosphide routes, unusually stable molecular clusters accumulate instead of turning immediately into a smoothly growing distribution. Their appearance breaks the simple link between mixing the precursor and forming the final nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Two-Step Nucleation and Growth of InP Quantum Dots via Magic-Sized Cluster Intermediates
